newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks rally strongly on political twists.
newsitem.headline: India stocks rally strongly on political twists.

text.p: Indian shares rebounded sharply at mid-session on Friday as an ongoing political crisis took surprising twists towards a possible swift resolution, traders said.
Leaders of the ruling United Front and ally-turned-foe, the Congress party, said they were holding talks amid rising hopes of finding a successor to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index jumped 45.87 points, or 1.27 percent, to 3644.24 -- nearly four percent up from its early low of 3512.05.
"The knee jerk reaction was swift and upwards," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian partner of Goldman Sachs & Co.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's comment that he was confident the federal budget for 1997/98 would be passed also brightened the mood, traders said.
"The mood is upbeat," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Politicians said a consensus candidate for the prime minister's post could be named by the United Front before a vote of confidence scheduled for later on Friday, or soon afterwards.
"If the parties reach a consensus it will be very good for the market," Kotak's Jhaveri said.
Prices skidded in early trade as it appeared that the government faced almost certain defeat in a key parliamentary confidence vote after talks to defuse a political crisis broke down.
"The key issue for the market is whether the budget will be passed. It's almost become an independent issue," said Rupa Bose, strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in Singapore.

The Congress party's withdrawal of vital support for Deve Gowda's coalition on March 30 raised fears the market-friendly budget proposed by Chidambaram a month earlier, and still unapproved by parliament, would be a casualty if the government was ousted.
Deve Gowda on Friday moved a vote of confidence in his government before the lower house of parliament.
"We are asking investors to wait and watch for things to take shape," said Sanjeev Mohta, head of research at securities firm James Capel B&K. "The main issue remains the budget."

Congress has ordered its 140 deputies to vote against the motion. Opposition rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies, with 193 votes, have also decided to vote against Deve Gowda.
But the BJP sought to allay fears in the business community by promising to help pass the budget after the vote.
"We are a responsible party," said BJP spokeswoman Sushma Swaraj. "We can't trifle with the economic agenda of the nation."
Bose at Paribas Capital said stock markets were likely to remain volatile.
"The markets will see a bit of a roller coaster ride but if the index goes below 3000-3200 points, I would call a buy. I see no reason to panic," she said.
